2: Change¨There are two main types of change that matter can undergo:¤Physical Change –Matter changes form but not chemical identity
Water Boiling, freezing, ice being chopped, metal being bent¤Chemical Change –Matter undergoes a chemical reaction
Wood burning, food being cooked, iron rusting
explanation: Matter can undergo two primary types of change: physical changes and chemical changes. A physical change occurs when matter changes its physical form or state but retains its original chemical identity; examples include water boiling or freezing, ice being chopped, or metal being bent. In contrast, a chemical change involves a chemical reaction where matter is transformed into new substances with different chemical properties; examples include wood burning, food being cooked, or iron rusting.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of a chemical change?
questions.exp: Wood burning is a chemical change because a chemical reaction occurs, transforming wood into new substances (ash, gases). Boiling, chopping ice, and bending metal are physical changes.

questions.q: What is the defining feature of a physical change?
opts: Matter changes its form but not its chemical identity.
questions.exp: During a physical change, the form or state of the matter changes, but its chemical identity remains unchanged.
